name: Bengali Alur Dom
subtitle: baby potatoes sealed in a tangy yogurt and ginger gravy, the standard partner to luchi

ingredients.note: 1 tsp for the tempering, 1/2 tsp dry-roasted for the finish
one for the tempering, one dry-roasted for the finish
use compounded-free hing to keep the dish gluten-free

prepNotes: Boil the potatoes only until a fork goes in with slight resistance, then peel and prick them all over with a fork so the gravy gets inside.
Dry-roast 1/2 tsp cumin seeds and one dried chilli in a pan until they smell toasty, then grind them to a coarse powder. This bhaja moshla goes in at the very end and is what makes it taste Bengali.
Whisk the yogurt smooth and leave it at room temperature for 20 minutes before you begin.

steps.text: Heat the mustard oil to smoking point in a kadhai and let it settle off the heat for 30 seconds.
Fry the boiled potatoes with 1/4 tsp turmeric and a pinch of salt over medium heat for 6 to 7 minutes, until the skins are blistered and gold all over, then lift them out.
steps.tip: Dry the potatoes properly first or they will spit and refuse to colour.

steps.text: Add the bay leaf, 1 tsp cumin seeds and one dried chilli to the oil and let them crackle for 20 seconds, then stir in the asafoetida.
Fry the ginger paste for 1 minute, until it loses its raw smell.
Add the pureed tomato with the remaining turmeric, kashmiri chilli, cumin and coriander powders and cook 6 minutes, until the oil separates cleanly at the sides.
Pull the pan off the heat, beat in the whisked yogurt, then set it back on the lowest flame and cook 3 minutes without boiling.
steps.tip: If it looks grainy, take it off and whisk hard; it will come back together.

steps.text: Return the potatoes with the sugar, salt and slit chillies and turn them in the masala for 3 minutes so every one is coated.
Add the water, bring to a simmer, then cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes.
steps.tip: A tight lid is the point of dum: the potatoes finish in trapped steam, not in liquid.

steps.text: Uncover, raise the heat and reduce for 3 minutes until the gravy clings to the potatoes rather than pooling.
Stir through the garam masala, the ghee and the roasted bhaja moshla, cover and rest 5 minutes before serving.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and tastes better on day two. Reheat on low with a splash of water and add the bhaja moshla fresh if you have it.
